In this instalment of Stable Tours, TTR catches up with Sterling Alexiou, who trains in partnership with Gerald Ryan, to look ahead to an exciting spring, with established stars Chilly Girl and Skyhook heading the team but joined by a host of promising youngsters, including an exciting fresh crop of 2-year-olds.

Everest record-setter Yes Yes Yes added a 12th black-type performer to his record on Saturday when Oh Yes She Did flew home to finish third in the G3 Quezette Stakes. With over 20 metropolitan winners last season and Group 1 performer Affirmative Action en route to the G1 Proisir Plate, there is plenty to keep the connections of Gooree Park's quiet achiever excited this spring.

At Warwick Farm on Tuesday Jokers Grin landed a close Warwick Farm open heat full of talent, with Oh Diamond Lil and Weeping Woman also impressing , Fovea and Laconic Livo emerged as two of the more impressive maiden and Class 1 winners.

Fireworks closed out the 2026 Arqana August Yearling Sale when a son of Wootton Bassett was knocked down to Coolmore for a French record of €4.6 million on Monday. The sale saw a 10.4% increase in gross from the 2025 edition of the sale, with long-time leading consignor Ecurie des Monceaux accounting for 30% of the total.

In this instalment of Stable Tours, TTR catches up with Adrian Bott to fill us in on where the stars of Tulloch Lodge are aimed this spring. The Waterhouse-Bott team will have several 3-year-olds on a G1 Golden Rose Stakes path and Sir Delius is out to firm his stallion credentials with a G1 Cox Plate.

The Thoroughbred Report touched base with industry professionals to see who caught their eye at the weekend’s Victorian stallion parades at Darley, Lovatsville, Swettenham, Widden, Woodside Park, and Yulong. Southport Tycoon, Diego Velazquez, Vinrock, and Espionage were among those who got several mentions.

Godolphin were dominant again on the second day of the Arqana August Yearling Sale, with a €2.4 million Wootton Bassett colt featuring amongst four seven-figure lots bought by the operation on Sunday. A Siyouni half-brother to Diamond Necklace is bound for Japan and Chaldean topped the first season sires with an average of €275,000.

For Oscar Englebrecht, joining Lustre Lodge marks a fresh chapter, bringing together lessons from experience at some of Australia’s leading studs with a boutique operation focused on quality, accessibility and future investment in breeding and racing opportunities.
